design_rationale:
WORKLOG - task 1 of financing_plan_desk (Belrose Fine Jewelers, promotional financing).

STEP 0. THE DRAW, THE LEDGER OF WHAT IS OCCUPIED, AND THE CLAIM.
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/tasks/financing_plan_desk --task 1
  {"task": 1, "key": "fine_jewelry_retailer/financing_plan_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4, 6]}
So this task is a tree of four problems, three of them prerequisites, and the four computations carry
6, 4, 4 and 6 factors. Assignment made by the author: the schedule rebuild takes 6, the hardship
arrangement 6, the cycle statement 4 and the service-recovery give-back 4.
Occupied by task 0: financing_ext_settlement_figure, financing_ext_returned_payment_charge and
financing_ext_lateness_charge, with the tools confirm_plan_settlement_d71750ce,
book_returned_payment_charge_6a9e81de and book_lateness_charge_0092ea40; base policies
financing_closure_and_payoff, financing_evt_payment_allocation, financing_evt_returned_payment and
financing_evt_late_fee were read there as lineage. Claimed here: financing_ext_cycle_statement,
financing_ext_service_recovery_giveback, financing_ext_schedule_rebuild and
financing_ext_hardship_schedule, with issue_cycle_statement_c71da302,
apply_service_recovery_giveback_b70a9c9e, update_scheduled_payment_2c04479a and
confirm_hardship_schedule_eb08e7db. The two scopes are pairwise disjoint in policies and in tools,
and together they cover all seven extended policies, which is what the final run of check_extended
asserts. Task 0 books charges onto a past-due plan and settles it; this task services a running
plan - it closes a cycle, puts right a charge the chain's own instruction caused, rebuilds what the
plan bills and puts the customer onto an arrangement. No policy, tool or event type is shared.

A SCOPE REVISION, RECORDED IN FULL.
The first draft of this task made the root's second-hop prerequisite a merchandise return credit:
the customer brings a pair of earrings back, the credit is posted, the schedule is rebuilt on the
smaller balance. Symptom: the prerequisite was undiscoverable. Root cause: nothing in the records
shows that a return has been accepted - the acceptance would itself be the entry the credit creates -
so the only way an agent could learn of it was for the customer to say so, and a prerequisite the
customer conveys is exactly what principle H forbids, while a persona fact with no seed row behind
it is what principle E forbids. Change: that policy was withdrawn from the charter and replaced by
financing_ext_cycle_statement, whose unmet state is plainly visible - the plan's statement day is
the fifth, a cycle closed on 2026-09-05, and the billing history carries statements closed
2026-07-05 and 2026-08-05 and nothing after. The rebuild's first edge was re-pointed at it and its
gate moved from the balance binding to the interest binding, because what a missing statement
changes is the closing date the cycle's interest is anchored on. Propagated in the same pass: the
rebuild's balance reading was re-cut to read give-backs rather than merchandise credits (so the
give-back edge still carries a value), the hardship policy's interest binding was re-cut the same
way, the task tool was renamed and re-signatured, and the whole thing was re-run. Result: all four
per-task gates green.

WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST.
The caller asks one thing - put me on something smaller - and names no number. Three things have to
be put right before that figure can even be worked out, and none of them is mentioned by him: a
closed cycle carries no statement, a lateness charge stands although the chain's own automatic
payment instruction is what failed, and the payment the plan bills still answers the amount financed
two and a half years ago rather than what is owed now. Each is found only by reading the records
against the published rules, each is resolved by a different write, and the order is forced: the
statement and the give-back in either order, then the rebuild, then the arrangement. The four
figures rest on twenty declared factors across four other registers - care coverage, a bench work
order, a design studio commission - and on seventeen ledger entries over thirty-one months.

STEP 0 CARDS.
Base-invariant card.
 - Subject financing_statement_issued -> the only governing base policy is
   financing_evt_statement_cycle, whose one applicable gate is plan_billing: "A statement is
   produced only while that plan stands at active, past due or in a hardship arrangement, and only
   when the balance reaches the smallest balance the term produces a statement for." Authority
   system_record, correlation key financing_plans.financing_plan_id bound to the call's
   financing_plan_id. Satisfied: the plan stands active and carries 5,240.00, far above the term's
   1.00 statement threshold. No time gate applies to this subject.
 - Subject financing_fee_waiver_applied -> financing_courtesy_waiver, two applicable gates.
   one_giveback_per_charge is a dedup gate on financing_ledger.source_entry_id: satisfied because
   the only two give-backs on the plan name the lateness charges of 2025-11-20 and 2026-05-12, not
   the 2026-09-08 charge this call answers. minimum_courtesy_tenure is a time gate: anchor "the date
   the plan began billing", source financing_plans.activated_date, relation not_before, duration
   variants.courtesy_waiver_minimum_tenure_months (nine months on this term), unit calendar months,
   boundary inclusive, counted with the anniversary rule quoted verbatim in temporal_feasibility.
   Positive case: billing began 2024-02-10, so the ninth whole month completed 2024-11-10 and the
   handling date is thirty-one whole months past it. Negative case: on 2024-11-09 the ninth month is
   not complete and no give-back may be granted.
 - Subjects financing_plan_terms_updated and financing_hardship_enrolled -> financing_hardship_
   arrangement, one applicable gate, plan_servicing_state, allowing active, past due or an
   arrangement being replaced. Satisfied: the plan stands active with no arrangement in force.
 - No eligibility of any governing policy is weakened. Four base handling clauses are superseded,
   each declared clause by clause in its own policy's overwrite block: the scheduled-payment
   sentence of financing_evt_statement_cycle, the own-reason give-back sentence of
   financing_courtesy_waiver (whose meaning about not consuming the courtesy allowance is carried
   into the replacing sentence), the schedule-recalculation sentence of financing_return_credit, and
   the reduced-payment sentence of financing_hardship_arrangement. Everything else stays in force.
Business-object card.
 The statement attaches to one closed cycle, identified by the closing date of 2026-09-05, which is
 the plan's own statement day; the two cycles already stated, 2026-07-05 and 2026-08-05, are
 excluded by their own entries. The give-back attaches to one priced charge, the lateness charge
 booked 2026-09-08, written into the new entry's source entry, so it can never be read as answering
 the charges of 2026-08-10, 2026-05-12 or 2025-11-20 - and the last two of those are themselves
 already answered, by the give-backs of 2025-11-28 and 2026-05-20, which name them as their source
 entries. The rebuild and the arrangement attach to the one promotional financing plan this customer
 holds. Rows entering the charge sums: lateness charges and give-backs on this plan inside the
 stretch each policy's own reading selects; rows excluded: purchases, statements and payments.
Problem-tree card.
 Root: financing_ext_hardship_schedule (confirm_hardship_schedule_eb08e7db, owner user).
 Prerequisites: financing_ext_schedule_rebuild (update_scheduled_payment_2c04479a, owner agent),
 and beneath it financing_ext_cycle_statement (issue_cycle_statement_c71da302, owner agent) and
 financing_ext_service_recovery_giveback (apply_service_recovery_giveback_b70a9c9e, owner agent).
 Shape: a chain from the root into the rebuild, which then fans out into two. Three prerequisite
 problems, exactly the draw; at least max(3-1,1) = 2 value_input edges are required and all three
 edges are value_input.
 Edge 1 - hardship -> rebuild, kind value_input, gate ordinary_payment, form state. Prerequisite
   sentence, verbatim from the hardship policy's own rule: "The reduced payment is worked out only
   once the scheduled monthly payment the plan record carries answers the balance the plan owes at
   the handling date." Four-point test: (1) "only once" joins the policy's own result to what it
   waits on; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state - the scheduled monthly payment standing on
   the plan record, named in the words the plan table and its finder use; (3) no tool, no policy id,
   no code token; (4) a hard requirement, scoped exactly to that one field. Exactly one write in
   this difficulty brings that state about: only financing_ext_schedule_rebuild writes the plan's
   billed payment, which its own rule states in its own terms. Derivation: the sentence says the
   billed payment must answer the balance; the records show 344.72 standing against a balance of
   5,240.00, which is the term's factor on the 12,400.00 originally financed and not on what is
   owed; the rebuild policy is the one rule that produces a payment from the balance now owed; so
   that write, and no other, resolves it.
 Edge 2 - rebuild -> cycle statement, kind value_input, gate interest_component, form state.
   Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from the rebuild's own rule: "The rebuilt payment is fixed only
   after every billing cycle the plan has closed carries in the billing history the statement that
   cycle presented." Ordering connective "only after"; the XX side is a record-visible state - a
   closed cycle carrying its statement entry; no tool, id or code token; scoped to every closed
   cycle. Exactly one write brings it about: only financing_ext_cycle_statement books a statement.
 Edge 3 - rebuild -> service-recovery give-back, kind value_input, gate balance_now, form state.
   Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from the rebuild's own rule: "Before the rebuilt payment is
   worked out, every lateness charge the plan carries that a failure of the chain's own handling
   brought about must already stand answered by a give-back in the billing history." Ordering
   connective "Before"; the XX side is a record-visible state - a lateness charge carrying a
   give-back against it; no tool, id or code token; scoped exactly to charges the chain's own
   handling brought about. Exactly one write brings it about: only
   financing_ext_service_recovery_giveback books a give-back under that ground.
 Topological order: statement, give-back, rebuild, arrangement. The first two are parallel and
 commute; see prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness.
 Deletion sensitivity, from the Step 5 run: skip the statement and the rebuilt payment goes to
 252.59; skip the give-back and it goes to 205.94; skip the rebuild and the reduced payment goes to
 224.41. All three edges bear weight.
 Nothing in the tree waits on an event outside the conversation: a statement is a book entry, a
 give-back is a book entry, the billed payment is a field on the plan, and the arrangement is a
 commitment the customer makes on the telephone.

STEP 1. THE POLICIES.
financing_ext_cycle_statement (state_due; the statement is owed at month-end whether or not anyone
rings). Baseline: the payment due for the cycle is the scheduled monthly payment, the charges read
are those of the two whole months ending on the handling date taken whole, nothing for coverage,
added and rounded. Four factors: the payment-due reading (method), the presented-charge window
(method, a window convention), the presentation share (parameter) and the coverage presentation band
(parameter, cross-difficulty on protection).
financing_ext_service_recovery_giveback (state_due). Baseline: the charges answered are the lateness
charges of the term's repeat window, no addition for repeated failure, none for the workshop. Four
factors: the charge reading window (method), the answered-charge selection (method, a selection
rule), the repeated-failure addition (parameter) and the workshop addition (parameter,
cross-difficulty on service).
financing_ext_schedule_rebuild (state_due). Baseline: the term's payment factor on the balance as
the plan record carries it adjusted over the repeat window, plus one cycle's interest at the term's
promotional rate on a thirty-day cycle and a 365-day year, no catch-up, nothing for coverage. Six
factors: the payment factor (parameter), the interest rate (parameter), the balance adjustment
reading (method), the cycle interest convention (method, a day-count convention), the missed-cycle
catch-up (parameter) and the carried coverage amount (parameter, cross-difficulty on protection).
financing_ext_hardship_schedule (on_request; a replacement schedule arises only because the customer
asks). Baseline: the term's hardship share of the payment the plan bills, over the term's hardship
length, no interest, the desk's standard arrangement charge, no relief. Six factors: the arrangement
length (method), the arrangement payment basis (method), the hardship share (parameter), the
arrangement interest band (parameter), the arrangement charge band (parameter) and the relief for
other commitments (parameter, cross-difficulty on custom).
Multi-source floor: the task needs one and carries several - the presentation share and the coverage
presentation band, the repeated-failure and workshop additions, the rebuild's payment factor and
interest rate, and the arrangement's payment basis, charge band and commitment relief each combine
two conditions over distinct evidence on every tier beyond the fall-through.
Cross-difficulty floor: the task needs one and carries four, reading three difficulties' registers -
protection twice (the coverage's standing, its premium arrangement, its allowance and its
deductible), service once (the work order's standing, the date promised and the rework count) and
custom once (the commission's stage and its balance). Every one reads a value, not a bare existence.
Forward and reverse sweep rule <-> compute_basis <-> compute: every binding that reads the world,
aggregates, branches, caps or rounds carries a verbatim rule quotation - fifteen on the statement,
sixteen on the give-back, twenty-one on the rebuild, fifteen on the arrangement. Swept back, every
load-bearing sentence of each rule is claimed by a binding: the window sentences by
charge_window_months, adjust_window_months and arrangement_months; the ladder sentences by their
ladder bindings; the combination and rounding semantics are pinned in prose in each policy ("the
share is applied to the line's value first" in the statement policy's sibling, "the hardship share
is applied to the payment the arrangement is built on and that figure is rounded to the cent; the
interest and the arrangement charge are then added to it and the relief is taken off; the result is
rounded to the cent at the end only"). No sentence is unclaimed and no filter is unquoted.

STEP 2. THE TOOLS.
Capability contract cards, written before the code.
 issue_cycle_statement_c71da302 - owner agent, rw write. Target: one plan's billing history. Atomic
 action: create one statement entry carrying the amount presented, the closing date as its posting
 date, the month of the closing date as its cycle, and the date the money falls due. Observable: the
 customer sees the statement and what it asks for. Receipt: one sentence naming the new entry, the
 plan, the closing date, the due date and the amount.
 apply_service_recovery_giveback_b70a9c9e - owner agent, rw write. One give-back entry, negative,
 booked under the service-recovery ground against the priced charge it answers, allocated to fees.
 Receipt: one sentence naming the new entry, the plan, the charge answered and the money given back.
 update_scheduled_payment_2c04479a - owner agent, rw write. One field on the plan record: the
 payment it bills each cycle. Nothing else moves and no entry is booked. Receipt: one sentence
 naming the plan and the payment now standing on it.
 confirm_hardship_schedule_eb08e7db - owner user, rw write, because committing to a replacement
 schedule is a promise about the customer's own money and the blueprint reserves it to them. The
 plan record moves into its arrangement standing, records which arrangement is in force and bills
 the reduced figure. Receipt: one sentence naming the plan, the arrangement and the payment.
None of the four reads anything, tests anything or returns a policy refusal. The posting date and
the cycle of the give-back come from the clock inside the tool; the statement's posting date is the
closing date the agent passes, because a statement is dated by the cycle it closes and not by the
day the desk gets to it. Gate run after writing them:
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_task_tools.py env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/tasks/financing_plan_desk
  -> TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK (7 tools)

STEP 3. THE WORLD, AND WHY EACH CLASS OF ROW IS THERE.
One customer, one plan on the 36-Month Equal Payment Plan, seventeen ledger entries, one finance
desk request, and one holding in each of three other difficulties.
 - The plan (active, automatic payment in force, no arrangement, billing since 2024-02-10, balance
   5,240.00, billing 344.72, statement day the fifth). The active standing plus automatic payment is
   what puts the world off the fall-through tier of the presentation share, the payment factor, the
   interest rate and the interest convention; make automatic payment false and four factors fall
   back to their baselines at once. The statement day is what makes the missing cycle visible.
 - Two purchase entries, 12,400.00 on 2024-02-01 and 1,980.00 on 2026-08-02, which is why the
   balance is what it is after thirty-one months of payments.
 - Six settled automatic payments from 2026-03-05 to 2026-08-05, all on the automatic payment
   channel, which is the evidence that the instruction ran cleanly until it did not. None of them
   falls in the month ending on the handling date, which is why the statement's payment-due reading
   takes the returned-payment tier rather than the settled-payment one.
 - Two statements, closed 2026-07-05 and 2026-08-05, each printing a due date twenty-five days
   later. They are the near-miss of the whole task: they make it look as though the plan is stated
   up to date, and only the statement day on the plan record shows that a third cycle closed on
   2026-09-05 and carries nothing. Delete either and the anchor the rebuild's interest moves from is
   wrong.
 - The returned automatic payment of 2026-09-01. It is the evidence of the chain's own instruction
   failing, and it moves five separate tiers: the statement's payment due, the statement's charge
   window, the give-back's charge window, the rebuild's catch-up and the arrangement's payment basis
   and charge band. Delete it and the task loses most of its shape.
 - Four lateness charges and two give-backs, laid out so that the two window factors and the
   selection factor all bite. The charge of 2026-08-10 sits at one whole month from the handling
   date: inside the statement's two-month baseline reading and outside its one-month world reading,
   which is exactly the near-miss that separates 19.00 from 38.00. The charge of 2025-11-20 and its
   part give-back of 2025-11-28 sit at nine months: inside the give-back's twelve-month world
   reading and outside its six-month baseline. The give-back of 2026-05-20 sits at three months:
   inside the rebuild's six-month baseline reading and outside its one-month world reading, which is
   what makes the balance adjustment factor bite. The give-back of 2025-11-28 is a part give-back of
   20.00 against a 41.00 charge, deliberately not a full one, so that the twelve-month and six-month
   readings of the answered charges cannot coincide.
 - The finance desk request of 2026-09-14, standing recorded and unconfirmed: the authority that an
   arrangement was asked for, and the reason the customer's confirmation is the thing that completes
   it.
 - Care coverage on the financed ring, in force, premium taken in one payment, no claim settled,
   2,500.00 allowance against a 50.00 deductible. Delete it and both the statement and the rebuild
   fall to their coverage baselines.
 - Work order WO-773915, in the workshop, promised 2026-09-01, rework count one. Delete it and the
   give-back falls by 40.00.
 - Commission CO-509314, in production, 6,020.00 still to pay. Delete it and the reduced payment
   rises by 15.00.
Automatic clauses checked row by row before seeding: the plan is active and current in standing, far
short of the term's thirty-day delinquency threshold on any unanswered due date, so no delinquency
marking or write-off is owed; the term is an equal-payment term holding no interest back, so nothing
about deferred interest can arise and accrued_promo_interest is 0.00; the promotional term runs to
2027-02-10; the coverage's next inspection falls 2026-11-20; the commission's delivery is promised
for 2026-11-20. No cache trap is designed here.
Prerequisites actively falsified: the cycle closed 2026-09-05 carries no statement; the lateness
charge of 2026-09-08 carries no give-back; the billed payment is the one struck at term start. All
three are false as a matter of seeded fact and all three flip true the moment their write lands.

STEP 4. THE PERSONA.
Tobias is written as the opposite of task 0's caller: fast, apologetic, a little scattered, thanking
people twice. He volunteers three things: the goal (a smaller payment he can manage, from the next
cycle, without stopping), the circumstance behind it (a tour that collapsed), and one natural aside
(the ring is still at the workshop past the date he was promised). All three are independently true
of the opening world - the plan is active and billing 344.72, and work order WO-773915 stands in the
workshop with a promised date of 2026-09-01 now passed. He gives his mobile and postal code only as
they are asked for, his date of birth and email if more is needed, and when asked what the plan
currently bills he says he could not tell them and would rather they read it off the account, which
is the must-ask question with a definite answer that never enters gold. He never mentions a
statement, a cycle, a charge, a give-back or the billed payment being out of date. His only
contribution on any prerequisite is passive: if the agent says the account must be brought up to
date first, he says of course. He asks to run the arrangement step himself, which is what hands the
customer's own tool over. His arc closes exactly where the evaluation closes: he reacts to the
confirmation that the plan is running on the arrangement and rings off, asking for nothing further.

STEP 5. VERIFICATION, ACTUALLY RUN.
The recomputation was run before any gold was filled in, using the gate's own evaluator on the
policies and the seed as they stand on disk, problem by problem on each problem's own handling-time
world. Commands and output:
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/tasks/financing_plan_desk --task 1
  task comps fact xfac hist brch step match
  1.json   4   20    4   16   64   16  True
  COMPUTE OK
Per problem:
  cycle statement, on the opening world: result 710.44; factor baselines 365.72, 729.44, 729.44,
    708.44; every-factor baseline 420.72.
  service-recovery give-back, on the opening world: result 160.00; factor baselines 139.00, 210.00,
    145.00, 120.00; every-factor baseline 114.00.
  schedule rebuild, on the world after both of those have landed: result 202.33; factor baselines
    221.63, 203.17, 201.49, 230.84, 144.88, 198.83; every-factor baseline 190.16.
  hardship arrangement, on the world after the rebuild has landed: result 160.33; factor baselines
    155.16, 129.31, 201.02, 109.57, 165.33, 175.33; every-factor baseline 128.90.
Every factor moves its result and every all-baseline figure differs from gold, so an agent who finds
only the computation documents computes four definite wrong numbers. The root was evaluated on the
post-prerequisite world: on the opening world its payment basis would read 344.72 off the plan
record and its figure would be 224.41, which is not gold.
Prerequisite sensitivity, run by skipping one write at a time and replaying the rest: skipping the
statement gives a rebuilt payment of 252.59 (the interest anchor falls back to 2026-08-05, forty-three
days instead of twelve); skipping the give-back gives 205.94 (the adjustment reading widens to the
term's six-month window, so the balance reads 5,210.00 instead of 5,080.00); skipping the rebuild
gives a reduced payment of 224.41. All three edges bear weight, which the gate's own value_input test
confirms independently.
Order test: both orders of the statement and the give-back were run and give the same two amounts and
the same terminal DB, because neither policy's compute reads the family of entry the other writes.
Whole-input floors: forcing every cross-category read off changes all four results; zeroing the
history aggregates changes all four.

STEP 6. EVALUATION AND CLOSURE.
Read nodes: locate, verify, then the plan, the whole ledger, the finance desk request, the care
coverage, the work order and the commission - eight reads, none duplicated, each feeding a named
factor or gate. The ledger read is the agent's path to two of the three prerequisites (the statements
that stop at 2026-08-05, and the lateness charge of 2026-09-08 with no give-back naming it), and the
plan read is the path to the third (344.72 standing against a balance of 5,240.00).
Write nodes in topological order: statement (step 9), give-back (step 11), rebuild (step 13), then
the arrangement, which the customer runs (step 15).
Closure: policy -> target tool -> computation step/arg -> gold call -> terminal state holds for all
four; set(computations.policy_id) equals charter_scope.extended_policies equals the tree;
required_documents repeats that list verbatim and in order; charter_scope.task_tools is the four
tools in first-call order.
Negative space proved rather than omitted: no lateness charge is booked here, because the due date of
2026-08-30 already carries the charge of 2026-09-08 and the due date printed on the statement issued
at step 9, 2026-09-30, has not yet arrived; no returned-payment charge is booked, because that is not
this task's territory and none is owed on the records read; and no further give-back is granted, the
term's allowance of two courtesy give-backs in a rolling twelve months being untouched because this
one is recorded under the service-recovery ground.
Reachability, turn by turn: he states the goal, the timing and the refusal to stop paying in his
first breath; he gives the mobile and the postal code when asked, which is exactly the two the
verification tool needs; the plan, the history, the request record and the three outside registers
are all reachable by the share finders; the agent explains the account has to be brought up to date,
he agrees; the three desk writes land synchronously; the agent hands him the arrangement step, he
runs it, and its real return - the plan, the arrangement and the payment - enters the shared
transcript; he reacts to that and closes. Everything happens under the one frozen time of
2026-09-17 14:05:00 EDT.

STEP 7. GATES RUN FOR THIS TASK, AND THE BLIND RE-DERIVATION.
  check_extended --task 1     -> EXTENDED OK
  check_task_tools            -> TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK
  replay_tasks --task 1       -> REPLAY OK (16 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous, 0 errors, closure 23 of 23)
  check_solvability --task 1  -> SOLVABILITY OK (4 calls, 5 base gates, 18 seed rows)
  check_compute --task 1      -> COMPUTE OK
  check_grounding --task 1    -> GROUNDING OK (2 identity attributes used, 4 answers, 4 writes, 8 conditional markers)
  check_cross_fire --task 1   -> SCOPE OK
  check_cache_diff --task 1   -> CACHE-DIFF INFO (no cache trap designed here)
Revisions recorded. (1) The scope revision above, from the merchandise return credit to the cycle
statement. (2) check_solvability failed on three citations whose snippets began "he wants" while the
persona sentence begins "He wants"; root cause: the snippets were typed rather than lifted; fixed by
quoting verbatim; re-run SOLVABILITY OK. (3) The first draft of edge_load_bearing asserted that
skipping the give-back would leave the balance at 5,240.00 and the payment at 208.71; the skip run
returned 205.94. Root cause: with no give-back in the month, the adjustment reading widens to the
term's six-month window and picks up the part give-back of 2026-05-20, so the balance reads 5,210.00.
The edge's flips_to_true_by and its skipped_effect were both corrected to that, and the same run
corrected the hardship edge's figure from 224.15 to 224.41.
Blind re-derivation, with the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier masked, from
only the prose that will be published, the tool schemas, the records a share finder returns and the
lines the persona can actually say: the plan is a 36-Month Equal Payment Plan standing active on
automatic payment, billing 344.72 against a balance of 5,240.00; its statement day is the fifth and
the history stops at the statement of 2026-08-05, so the cycle closed 2026-09-05 is unstated; the
automatic payment of 2026-09-01 came back and a lateness charge followed it on 2026-09-08 with
nothing answering it; the published rules say the rebuilt payment waits on both of those and the
reduced payment waits on the rebuilt payment. So: the statement comes to 689.44 plus 19.00 plus 2.00,
that is 710.44; the give-back to 105.00 plus 15.00 plus 40.00, that is 160.00; the rebuilt payment to
121.92 plus 19.46 plus 57.45 plus 3.50, that is 202.33; and the reduced payment to 122.07 plus 50.76
plus 2.50 less 15.00, that is 160.33. That is gold, by the same route and in the same order. No
second reading of the published text reaches a different figure: every branch turns on a record that
is either there or not there, and the three places a careless reader can go wrong - the one-month
against two-month charge reading, the twelve-month against six-month charge reading, and the
statement anchor the interest runs from - are exactly where the factors were placed.
user_scenario:
Tobias Reinholt-Marchetti is forty-two, a live-sound engineer who has mixed for touring bands out of Brooklyn for nineteen years. He talks the way he works: fast, friendly, a little scattered, apologising for taking up the time and then carrying straight on. The reason he is calling is that the autumn tour he was booked on collapsed three weeks ago, the next one does not start until the new year, and he simply cannot find the full payment on the Belrose plan for the ring this month or next. He is not asking to stop paying — he is adamant about that, and says so more than once. He wants to keep paying something every month, just something he can actually manage, and he wants it to start from the next cycle rather than being backdated or argued about. He telephoned the desk a few days ago and asked whether there was a smaller arrangement he could go onto; he was told it would be looked at, and this is him ringing back to get it settled.

He is happy for the agent to go through the plan and put whatever needs putting right on it before the figure is set, and he says so plainly if they ask for that leave. What he will not do is let someone else commit him: the arrangement is a promise about his own money, so when the agent offers to put it in place for him he says, politely, that he would rather press the button himself, and asks to be given the step.

He hands over his details one at a time as they are asked for. The mobile he gives is 2125553147. The postal code on the account is 11215. If more is wanted, his date of birth is 1983-11-02 and the email on file is t.reinholtmarchetti@harbourline.net. If he is asked what the plan is currently billing him he laughs and says he honestly could not tell them, the statements go to a folder he does not open, and he would rather they read it off the account than have him invent a number.

Somewhere in the middle he remembers to ask about the ring — it went to the workshop in August and he was promised it for the first of the month and it still is not back — and he asks whether that makes any difference to the plan. Whatever he is told about it, he lets it go and does not raise it again. If the agent explains that the account has to be brought up to date before the new payment can be worked out, he says of course, take whatever time it needs, he would rather it were done properly. If a figure is read to him he does not haggle and does not offer a figure of his own; he says that sounds like something he can hold to. Once the agent hands him the step to take the arrangement up, he runs it himself and reads back what it tells him. When he hears the plan is running on the arrangement, he thanks them twice, says that is a weight off, and rings off. He asks for nothing further.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the customer profile from the mobile number the caller states, fixing whose account the call concerns.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Without the profile reference there is no customer to verify and no plan to read; every later lookup is keyed on it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record that the caller cleared the identity check against two details held on the profile.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The plan's billing schedule is changed and an arrangement is taken on in this conversation, so the caller must first be proved to be the profile holder.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the customer's promotional financing plans: the term, the standing, the balance, the date billing began, the statement day, the scheduled payment, whether automatic payment runs and which arrangement if any is in force.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The term fixes every tier parameter read, the standing and the automatic payment flag decide four separate tiers, the statement day says which cycle has closed, and the balance and the scheduled payment are inputs of three of the four figures.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the plan's whole billing history: the financed merchandise, statements with their closing and due dates, payments and how each cleared, lateness charges and the give-backs already standing against them.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The statements show which closed cycle carries none, the returned automatic payment and the lateness charges decide the statement amount and the give-back, and the give-backs already booked decide both the charge selection and the balance the rebuilt payment rests on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the finance desk request record to find the arrangement request taken for this plan and the terms it was taken on.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: An arrangement is taken on the desk's request record and takes effect only once the customer confirms it, so the request record is the authority that one was asked for.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the customer's care coverage: the coverage held, whether it stands in force, the premium arrangement, the allowance still carried and the deductible.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The coverage amount presented on the statement and the coverage amount carried in the rebuilt payment are both decided from the coverage's standing, its premium arrangement, its allowance and its deductible.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the customer's bench work orders: the standing of the order, the date the piece was promised for and how many times it has been back to the bench.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The workshop addition on the give-back is decided from whether a piece is still with the workshop past the date it was promised for and whether it has been back to the bench.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the customer's design studio commissions: the stage the commission stands at and the balance still to pay on it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The relief allowed on the reduced payment for the customer's other commitments is decided from the commission's stage and whether a balance is still to pay.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.rebuilt_monthly_payment: 202.33 USD. The balance the payment is worked out on is 5,080.00: the plan record carries 5,240.00 and, because a give-back was booked to the plan in the whole month ending on the handling date, only the give-backs booked in that single month adjust it, which is the 160.00 booked at step 11 and not the 30.00 of 2026-05-20. The principal share is 121.92: the payment factor is the desk's steady-payer factor of 2.4 per cent, because automatic payment is in force and the plan has been billing thirty-one whole calendar months, at least the term's twelve-month repricing review length; 5,080.00 x 2.4 / 100 = 121.92. The interest one cycle carries is 19.46: the rate is the term's promotional rate of 11.99 per cent reduced by the term's automatic payment discount of 0.5 points, 11.49 per cent, because automatic payment is in force and only one payment has been sent back inside the review window, below the term's trigger of three; and because the plan stands active with automatic payment in force the interest runs on the actual days from the closing date of the most recent statement, 2026-09-05 as booked at step 9, to 2026-09-17, twelve days, on a year of three hundred and sixty days. The catch-up is 57.45: the plan stands active and a payment on it was sent back unpaid in the month ending on the handling date, so the scheduled monthly payment the plan record carries, 344.72, is spread evenly over the term's six-month arrangement length. The coverage amount carried is 3.50, the desk's coverage servicing amount, because the care coverage on the financed ring stands in force and the 2,500.00 allowance it still carries stands above its 50.00 deductible. 121.92 + 19.46 + 57.45 + 3.50 = 202.33, rounded to the cent.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.hardship_plan_code: reduced_payment. Basis: the tool's schema says, verbatim, 'Use reduced_payment when the customer keeps paying every cycle at a smaller figure'. Uniqueness: the customer says he is not asking to stop paying and wants to keep paying something every month that he can manage, which is exactly that situation. interest_pause would stop interest running rather than lower the payment, which is not what he asks for and not what the figure worked out expresses; payment_deferral would put whole cycles off to the end, which he explicitly refuses by insisting on paying every month; none would leave the plan on its ordinary schedule, which is the thing he cannot manage.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.reduced_payment_amount: 160.33 USD. The months the arrangement runs for are five: the plan stands active and has been billing thirty-one whole calendar months, at least the term's thirty-six month promotional length less its six-month hardship length, so the arrangement runs to the end of the promotional term, 36 less 31. The payment the arrangement is built on is 271.27: the scheduled monthly payment the plan record carries after step 13 is 202.33, which stands above the term's 65.00 floor, and a payment on the plan was sent back unpaid in the month ending on the handling date, so the 344.72 sent back is spread evenly over those five months, 68.94, and added. The hardship share is the desk's long-standing share of 45 per cent, because no arrangement stands in force and the plan began billing thirty-one whole calendar months ago, at least twice the term's twelve-month minimum hardship tenure: 271.27 x 45 / 100 = 122.07 rounded to the cent. The interest the arrangement carries is 50.76: exactly one payment has been sent back unpaid inside the term's twelve-month repricing review window, so the balance after the give-backs booked in the month ending on the handling date, 5,240.00 less 160.00 = 5,080.00, is taken at the term's promotional rate of 11.99 per cent for one month of a twelve-month year. The arrangement charge is 2.50, the desk's arrangement charge, because no arrangement stands in force and a payment was sent back unpaid in that month. The relief for other commitments is 15.00, the desk's larger commitment relief, because commission CO-509314 with the design studio stands in production with 6,020.00 still to pay. 122.07 + 50.76 + 2.50 - 15.00 = 160.33, rounded to the cent.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Presenting the statement books an entry whose closing date is 2026-09-05, so the most recent statement the interest reading anchors on moves from 2026-08-05 to 2026-09-05 and the interest one cycle carries falls from 69.72 to 19.46.

edges.condition: Every lateness charge entry on the plan that arose from a failure of the chain's own handling carries a give-back entry in the billing history whose source entry is that charge.
edges.policy_source: Before the rebuilt payment is worked out, every lateness charge the plan carries that a failure of the chain's own handling brought about must already stand answered by a give-back in the billing history.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The automatic payment instruction the plan runs on was presented on 2026-09-01 and came back unpaid, and a lateness charge of 38.00 was booked against the plan on 2026-09-08 in consequence. No give-back entry in the billing history names that charge as its source entry: the only two give-backs on the plan, booked 2025-11-28 and 2026-05-20, name the lateness charges of 2025-11-20 and 2026-05-12.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Booking the give-back creates an entry whose source entry is the 2026-09-08 charge, so the adjustment reading narrows to the give-backs of the month ending on the handling date and the balance the rebuilt payment is worked out on becomes 5,080.00 instead of the 5,210.00 the six-month reading gives.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites of the rebuild are parallel and may be run either way round. They commute, and both orders were run: the statement policy reads payments, lateness charges and the care coverage, and never give-backs; the give-back policy reads lateness charges, give-backs, payments and the work order, and never statements. So neither write enters the other's compute, both produce the same amounts in either order (710.44 and 160.00), and the two created rows have content-hashed ids built from their own arguments, so the terminal DB is identical either way. The rebuild is strictly after both, because its interest reading anchors on the statement just booked and its balance reading takes in the give-back just booked; and the arrangement is strictly after the rebuild, because the payment it is built on is read off the plan record the rebuild writes.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the rebuild leaves the plan record billing 344.72 instead of 202.33, so the payment the arrangement is built on becomes 413.66 instead of 271.27 and the reduced payment becomes 224.41 instead of 160.33.
Skipping the statement leaves the most recent statement at 2026-08-05, so the interest one cycle carries becomes 69.72 instead of 19.46 and the rebuilt payment becomes 252.59 instead of 202.33.

Skipping the give-back leaves the adjustment reading on the term's six-month repeat window, so the balance the rebuilt payment is worked out on is 5,210.00 instead of 5,080.00 and the rebuilt payment becomes 205.94 instead of 202.33.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona never mentions a statement, a cycle that has not been billed, a lateness charge, a give-back, a bounced automatic payment or the payment the plan bills being out of date. He says only that the tour collapsed, that he cannot find the full payment, that he wants to keep paying something smaller from the next cycle, and that the agent may put right whatever needs putting right - a blanket leave that names nothing. His only volunteered detail beyond the request is that the ring is still at the workshop past the date it was promised for, which bears on a factor of the give-back rather than on the existence of any prerequisite, and he asks only whether it makes any difference to the plan. Everything he contributes about any of the three prerequisites is a passive reaction after the agent has explained it.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: None of the four tools checks anything. issue_cycle_statement_c71da302 mints an id and calls ctx.create on the ledger with the arguments as given; apply_service_recovery_giveback_b70a9c9e does the same; update_scheduled_payment_2c04479a calls ctx.update on the plan record with the figure given; confirm_hardship_schedule_eb08e7db calls ctx.update with the standing, the arrangement code and the figure given. Every one of them would write exactly as faithfully with the prerequisites unresolved and with any amount passed to it. There is no ctx.find, no status test and no conditional return in any of the four function bodies, so a prerequisite left unresolved shows up only as a different terminal hash.
